title: Angkor Empire Marathon 2026 Review: What the 11th Edition Was Like
seo_title: Angkor Empire Marathon 2026 Review: Course, Humidity, Cut-offs
meta_description: Angkor Empire Marathon 2026 review: 6,500 runners, a flat loop from Angkor Wat through Siem Reap and the temples, 25°C and 100% humidity at the 4.30am start, water every 2 km, a 6h30 cut-off.
dek: What it was like to run Cambodia's temple marathon on 2 August 2026: the course from Angkor Wat through Siem Reap and out to Banteay Samre, saturated air before dawn, the aid and cut-offs, crowding where the races meet, and how fast the field runs.
verdict: Enter if you want a full marathon among the Angkor temples and can handle saturated tropical air. The 2026 race drew 6,500 runners, about 1,000 of them in the marathon, on a flat course with water every 2 km, electrolyte drinks at about half the stations and a six-and-a-half-hour limit. The catch is the air and the crowding: at the 4.30am start it was 25°C with a dew point of 25°C and 100% humidity, and 30°C by 9.30am, and runners reported 10 km runners blocking the road around the Bayon. Pace for the humidity, aim to finish before the heat builds after 8am, and expect to share the road inside Angkor Thom.

sections.heading: The Course: Town, Temples and Back Through Angkor Thom
paragraphs: The marathon is a single loop that starts and finishes in front of Angkor Wat [1]. On the official map it heads south first, into Siem Reap past the Grand Hotel at 5 km, the Royal Palace at 6 km and Preah Prom Roth pagoda at 7 km, then comes back north on the other side of the river, past Phsar Leu at 9 km, to Prasat Kravan at 17 km and Srah Srang at 19 km, and on to a U-turn near Banteay Samre between 25 and 26 km. The way back passes East Mebon, Pre Rup at 30 km, Ta Prohm at 32 to 34 km and Ta Keo, enters Angkor Thom by the Victory Gate at 36 km, goes round the Bayon and leaves by the South Gate for the last 2 km past Phnom Bakheng [1].

The organiser describes it as a flat course lined with old trees, passing around 17 temples, and the course map carries the AIMS certified-course logo [2][1]. A reporter who ran the 10 km described a canopy over the road from Angkor Wat to the South Gate, mist over the waterways, and macaques taking discarded water bottles from the road [3]. The marathon also runs through Siem Reap city and a village, Preah Dak [3].

The half marathon goes south to a U-turn below Angkor Wat, then east past Banteay Kdei and Ta Prohm and back through Angkor Thom; the 10 km runs north through Angkor Thom to a turn beyond the North Gate [1]. Distance boards are posted every 1 or 2 km on the right-hand side of the road [2].

sections.heading: The Weather: Saturated Air Before Dawn
paragraphs: Siem Reap-Angkor International Airport, roughly 40 km east of Angkor Wat, recorded 25°C at the 4.30am start with a dew point of 25°C, 100% humidity and a 1-knot wind [4]. It barely moved for two hours: still 25°C and 100% at 5.30am, when the half marathon started, and 26°C at 7am. Then it warmed: 28°C at 8.30am, 30°C with 75% humidity at 9.30am, and 31°C at 11am, when the marathon limit ran out [4].

A dew point of 25°C with 100% humidity means sweat does almost nothing to cool you, so the flat profile flatters less than it looks. A 25-year-old Cambodian who finished in 4:55 said the heat made the race really challenging, though the early part was run in tree-lined shade [3]. Runners' reviews after the race called it flat and very hot, and very tough conditions [5]. The NOCC's secretary general, by contrast, said the weather on the day was favourable [6].
The time you finish decides the race you get. A three-and-a-half-hour marathoner was done by 8am in 25°C to 27°C air; a five-hour runner finished at 9.30am at 30°C [4].

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The organiser promises water and electrolyte drinks every 2 km, with bananas at some stations [2]. On the 2026 map the marathon has water at every even kilometre from 2 km to 40 km, with an electrolyte drink beside it at 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 26, 28, 32 and 36 km. Medical tents stand at the finish, at Banteay Kdei, near 27 km and inside Angkor Thom; toilets are marked at several points [1]. The organiser says an ambulance follows the race and medical tuk-tuks patrol the course, and that anyone who cannot continue should wait on the spot to be picked up [1].

The marathon started at 4.30am, the half at 5.30am, the 10 km at 5.40am and the 3 km at 5.50am [3][7]. The limits are six hours 30 for the marathon, four hours for the half, two hours for the 10 km and 45 minutes for the 3 km [7]. The marathon limit was cut from seven hours in 2025 [8]; in the 2025 results, 27 of the 373 marathon finishers took longer than 6:30 [9]. Full and half marathon runners must be 16 or over, and 10 km runners 13 or over [7].
Every finisher gets a medal and an e-certificate, and free food and drink at the finish [2]. Marathon and half-marathon finishers also get a finisher T-shirt [7].

sections.heading: What Went Wrong: Crowding at the Bayon and a Thin Finish
paragraphs: The four races share roads inside Angkor Thom, where the 10 km, half and marathon all pass the Bayon [1]. One runner wrote after the 2026 race that some 10 km runners were blocking faster marathon and half-marathon runners there, and suggested volunteers keep a lane open [5]. The same runner said the medical tent was set back from the finish line, no medics were visible at the line itself, and cramping runners were helped by other runners instead of medical staff. The 2-hour half-marathon pacer ran the first 3 km at about 5:15 per km and finished in about 1:56 [5].

A 10 km runner reported no portable toilets on that route, only one or two public toilets, and said the results first appeared with the previous year's date before being corrected that evening [5]. The first reviewer still called it an amazing experience, and the second said they would like to come back [5].
The previous edition was disrupted: the 2025 race, set for 3 August, was postponed because of the conflict on the Thai-Cambodian border [10] and was run on 31 August [11].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: About 1,000 people started the marathon, 1,000 the half, 3,000 the 10 km and 1,500 the 3 km [3]. In all, 6,500 runners from 51 countries took part, 1,050 of them from abroad, with the most from China, Japan and the UK [12][13].

Cambodia's Vann Pheara won the marathon in 2:41:08 and Kan Sreyroth the women's race in 3:10:57, ahead of China's Liu Haiping in 3:13:48, according to the results released by the NOCC [14]. Vann Pheara also won in 2024 and 2025 [15][11].

The full 2026 results had not been published on the organiser's results database by late September; the set posted there is from 2025 [9]. That year the marathon had 373 finishers, only 33 of them women. Tenth place was 3:36:13 for men and 4:54:36 for women, the third woman ran 3:42:55, and the median finisher took 5:02:32; only 37 finished inside four hours [9]. In a field like that, a 3:30 marathoner would have been in the top ten men, and a woman able to run 3:45 close to the podium.
In the 2025 half marathon the median finisher took 2:36:08 [9].

sections.heading: Race-Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Packs were collected at the Royal Angkor Resort, on the outskirts of Siem Reap, on Friday 31 July from 9am to 6pm and Saturday 1 August from 9am to 8pm [3][7][2]. There was no collection on race day; someone else can collect for you with a signed authorisation and copies of your confirmation and passport photo [7]. The pack held the bib, a T-shirt, a drawstring bag and a lanyard [3].

The start is about 6 km from the town, 20 minutes by tuk-tuk [2]. Runners were asked to be there at least 30 minutes before their start [7]; in 2026 runners and spectators began arriving at 3.30am, and volunteers had been on site since 2am [3].

In 2026 foreign runners paid US$60, US$65 or US$75 for the marathon depending on when they entered, and Cambodians US$30 to US$40, plus a 7% handling fee [7][2]. Entries closed on 25 June for individuals and 20 June for groups. Entries cannot be refunded or transferred, and changing distance costs US$20 [7].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want to run a full marathon through the Angkor park and do not mind a slow time. It is not the same race as the Angkor Wat International Half Marathon, a separate NOCC event held around the temples each December [3]. The 2026 field grew to 6,500, which the minister in charge of sport put at 25% more than in 2025 [12].

Think twice if you want a personal best, cannot cope with near-saturated air, or need a slick operation at the finish. If you run the marathon, expect congestion where the 10 km crosses your route around the Bayon [5].
AIMS lists the 2027 race for Sunday 8 August [10]. Entry fees, start times and cut-offs for 2027 had not been published when this was written.

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race information and course map, the 2025 results, airport weather records, English and Khmer news reports, a first-hand newspaper feature and runners' own reviews.

faqs.question: How hot and humid is the Angkor Empire Marathon?
faqs.answer: Very humid. At the 4.30am start in 2026, Siem Reap-Angkor airport recorded 25°C, a dew point of 25°C and 100% humidity with almost no wind. It stayed near 25°C until about 7am, then rose to 28°C by 8.30am and 31°C by 11am, when the marathon limit ran out. Pace for the humidity, not the flat course.

faqs.question: What are the cut-offs at the Angkor Empire Marathon?
faqs.answer: In 2026, six hours 30 minutes for the marathon, four hours for the half marathon, two hours for the 10 km and 45 minutes for the 3 km. The marathon limit was seven hours in 2025. In the 2025 results, 27 of the 373 marathon finishers took longer than six hours 30.

faqs.question: Is the Angkor Empire Marathon course flat?
faqs.answer: Yes. The organiser calls it a flat course lined with old trees, passing around 17 temples, and the map carries the AIMS certified-course logo. The marathon runs south through Siem Reap, east to a turn near Banteay Samre, then back past Pre Rup and Ta Prohm and through Angkor Thom to finish at Angkor Wat.

faqs.question: How many water stations does the Angkor Empire Marathon have?
faqs.answer: About 20 on the marathon. The organiser promises water and electrolyte drinks every 2 km, with bananas at some stations, and the 2026 map shows water at every even kilometre and electrolyte drinks at nine points. Medical tents stand at four places, with first-aid tuk-tuks and an ambulance following the race.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to place at the Angkor Empire Marathon?
faqs.answer: Not very. The 2026 winners ran 2:41:08 and 3:10:57. In 2025, the latest year with full results, tenth place was 3:36:13 for men and 4:54:36 for women, and only 37 of 373 finishers broke four hours. The median finisher took 5:02:32.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 to the review template, about the 11th edition run on 2 August 2026. Weather is from airport METAR observations, not a forecast. The full 2026 results had not been published: the organiser's results database holds the 2025 results under a 2027 date label, so field depth is from 2025 and labelled as such; 2026 winners are from the NOCC via China Daily Asia. Start times for the shorter races differ between the organiser's tables, map and the Ministry of Tourism; the times reported by the SCMP reporter on the day, which match the main registration table, are used. The organiser's own page gives the date as Sunday 3 August 2026; every other source gives 2 August. Foreign participation is 1,050 in NOCC figures and 900 in the technical director's pre-race figure; NOCC's figure is used. The 25% growth figure is attributed to the minister because CambodgeMag's 2025 figure of 4,224 implies more. Pack collection venue: SCMP and the organiser say the Royal Angkor Resort; a World's Marathons FAQ names a different hotel and looks stale. The runner reviews are named only by platform. No rating.
